Hi Sarah — quick answers inline and a concrete proposal below.

1) Burst handling: we can support transient 5x bursts but there are two paths:
   - Option A (no commit): Allow bursts up to 2x sustained with elastic routing; for 5x bursts we require a temporary quota increase request which is handled within 2 business days for standard accounts. For customers on Dedicated/reserved pools we can enable faster (minutes) autoscale.
   - Option B (recommended): A lightweight reserved capacity buffer (10–20% headroom) + short-term burst credits that auto-kick in when traffic exceeds quota. This gives sub-minute failover and predictable unit pricing for bursts.

2) Overage pricing: our standard overage banding is tiered:
   - Up to 10% over committed monthly quota: +20% unit price
   - 10–50% over: +50% unit price
   - >50% over: custom rate (we can cap with a negotiated step-down)

3) Minimum term for reserved capacity: 3 months for pilot reserved pools, 12 months for production commitments. Billing can be split (base reserved invoice + metered overage invoice).

Concrete example (for your numbers):
- Committed: 200M tokens/mo at $900 per 1M tokens = $180k/mo (example committed price)
- Reserved buffer: +20% headroom (40M tokens) included
- Overage bands: first 20M overage billed at $1,080 per 1M (20% premium), next up to 100M billed at $1,350 per 1M (50% premium).
- Burst credits: for short 5x bursts we can include a monthly pool of 10M burst tokens at the reserved rate; additional burst usage follows overage bands above.

I've attached a one-pager with this example and a sample invoice. If that looks OK, Rafael and I can draft an addendum with the exact bands to include in the MSA.

Next steps:
- Rafael: can you confirm whether we can front-load a 10M burst credit for a pilot (one-off) and the internal approval path for a temporary quota increase?
- Sarah / Mike: can you confirm the budget band you expect to land in (we quoted $10k–$25k/month earlier; above is a production-level example — want to make sure pricing aligns).

Thanks —
Marissa
